summary: Jörg Heimbel specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tibet University and completed his PhD at the University of Hamburg in 2014 under Franz-Karl Ehrhard and David P. Jackson. He has held posts at Hamburg, Munich, and Göttingen.
Jörg Plassen specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He has served as a professor at Geumgang University and at Ruhr University Bochum (attested 2013).

Jørn Borup was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Aarhus University (circa 1998–2002) under Armin W. Geertz and Ian Reader, later serving there as associate professor from around 2007 to 2023.
Jürgen Hanneder is an Indologist who completed his PhD at the University of Marburg under Michael Hahn in 1996. After posts at Bonn and Halle, he succeeded Hahn as professor at Marburg in 2007.

Jürgen Renn, a historian of science, earned his PhD at the Technical University of Berlin in 1987. He served as Director at the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science (1994) and Max Planck Institute of Geoanthropology (2022).

Jōryū Chiba (1921–2008) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history who studied at Ryukoku University. He spent his career there as lecturer, assistant professor, and professor emeritus (1970–1989), and directed the Honganji Historical Materials Research Institute (1983).

K. A. Nilakanta Sastri was a historian and Indologist who studied at Madras Christian College and the University of Madras. He held posts at Annamalai University (circa 1920–1922) and the University of Mysore (circa 1952–1956).
K. A. Subramania Iyer was an Indologist. He served as a professor at the University of Lucknow (attested 1972, 1987) and as Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.
K. Balasubrahmanya Iyer was an Indologist who served as managing editor of the Journal of Oriental Research and secretary of the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute (attested 1945).
K. Jayakumar is an Indologist and linguist educated at St. Joseph's Higher Secondary School, Thiruvananthapuram. He served in the Indian Administrative Service from around 1978 to 2012.
K. Kanapathypillai was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Hartley College and completed studies at the University of London between circa 1936 and 1940.

K. Kunjunni Raja was an Indologist and linguist who earned PhDs from the University of Madras and the University of London under John Brough. He served at the University of Madras and as honorary director of Adyar Library (1980–2005).

K. Meenakshi is an Indologist and linguist who earned her PhD from Savitribai Phule Pune University under Madhukar Anant Mehendale in 1964. She held a post at Jawaharlal Nehru University (attested 1983).

K. N. Jayatilleke was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Cambridge under Ludwig Wittgenstein. He later served as Senior Lecturer in Philosophy at the University of Ceylon from circa 1951 to 1963.

K. R. Norman was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. Educated at Downing College, Cambridge, he served on Cambridge's faculty from 1955 to 1992 and was President of the Pali Text Society from 1981 to 1994.

K. S. Balasubramanian is an Indology and philosophy scholar associated with the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, where he served on the editorial committee (attested 2001) and as director (attested 2026).

id: P:K. S. J. M. de Vreese
summary: K. S. J. M. de Vreese was an Indologist and linguist who served as a privaat-docent at Leiden University in 1948 and became a professor at the University of Amsterdam in 1960.

K. Srinivasan is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He has served as a professor at Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda College and held the Brahmasri Anna Subramaniam Chair at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute (attested 2020–2026).

K. T. S. Sarao is a Buddhist studies and history scholar. He earned PhDs from the University of Delhi and the University of Cambridge under Frank Raymond Allchin and K. R. Norman, becoming a professor at Delhi in 1995.
K. V. Puttappa was an Indologist who was educated at Hardwick High School and College, Maharaja's College, Mysore, and the University of Mysore.
